a group meeting to consider the feasibility of a new product
a group meeting to prepare the monthly financial reports
a group of workers pressing management for better pay

2024:Q50.explanation: An interest group forms because members share a common concern about a specific issue (e.g., pressing management for better pay). A group of friends listening to music is a Friendship Group. The other options are formal Task or Command groups.
2024:Q50.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Based on the definition of Interest Group on Slide 21.

2024:Q51.questionText: What is the core of making a plan?
2024:Q51.explanation: Planning is inherently future-oriented. It involves determining how the organization can get where it wants to go, which requires analyzing foreseen opportunities and thinking in advance.
2024:Q51.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the definition of planning on Slide 4 and the advantage 'Helps managers to be future-oriented' on Slide 6.

2024:Q52.questionText: Which of the following statements about groupthink is true?

options.content: Groupthink cannot take place in a newly formed group.
A group with high levels of mistrust and conflicts is likely to be most susceptible to groupthink.
A group with a high level of cohesiveness is likely to be susceptible to groupthink.
Managers must help committees to establish groupthink to generate alternative problem solutions.
A group which is highly competitive will most probably result in groupthink.

2024:Q52.explanation: Groupthink occurs when the "desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions." High cohesiveness creates this strong desire for agreement and conformity, making the group highly susceptible to groupthink.
2024:Q52.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition and symptoms of Groupthink on Slide 16.

2024:Q53.questionText: At what stage of the planning becomes the most feasible plan that can be implemented.
2024:Q53.explanation: After evaluating options, the manager chooses the best (most feasible) alternative to reach the objectives, which is then developed into actionable plans.
2024:Q53.reference: Chapter 8: Making Decisions - Slide 16 covers selecting the most beneficial alternative.

2024:Q54.questionText: ____ is the process of sharing information with other individuals.
2024:Q54.explanation: Communication is formally defined as the process of sharing information with other individuals.
2024:Q54.reference: Chapter 15: Influencing and Communication - Answer found on Slide 10.

2024:Q55.questionText: Planning establishes a ground standard for
2024:Q55.explanation: While planning is the basis for all functions, it specifically sets the organizational objectives and targets (standards) that the 'Controlling' function measures performance against to determine if goals are being met.
2024:Q55.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the 'Primacy of Planning' link to Controlling on Slide 7, and general management principles.

2024:Q56.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of division of labor?

options.content: It results in easier and more efficient work.
It broadens the scope of work.
It emphasizes the human variable in organizations.
It results in high levels of employee motivation.

2024:Q56.explanation: An explicit advantage of division of labor is that when workers concentrate on performing only one job, they naturally try to make the job easier and more efficient.
2024:Q56.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer found verbatim on Slide 12.

2024:Q57.explanation: In the context of the planning process, developing premises means formulating assumptions about future conditions and environments upon which the alternative plans will be based.
2024:Q57.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the planning definition on Slide 4 (assumptions about foreseen opportunities / future conditions).

2024:Q58.questionText: Which of the following is one of the three main components of the management system that Weber termed a bureaucracy?

options.content: close, personal relations among organization members

2024:Q58.explanation: Weber's bureaucratic model includes three main concepts: detailed procedures and rules, impersonal relationships, and a clearly outlined organizational hierarchy.
2024:Q58.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer found verbatim on Slide 9.

2024:Q59.questionText: An individual's emotional intelligence is characterized by self-awareness, self-motivation, self-regulation, empathy for others, and
2024:Q59.explanation: According to Goleman's concept of emotional intelligence, it encompasses managing own emotions as well as the emotions in relationships with others, which translates to an adeptness in building relationships.
2024:Q59.reference: Chapter 15: Influencing and Communication - Answer found on Slide 7.

2024:Q60.questionText: ____ is the mode of thinking that group members engage in when the desire for agreement so dominates the group that it overrides the need to realistically appraise alternative problem solutions.
2024:Q60.explanation: This is the exact definition of Groupthink provided in the lecture.
2024:Q60.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found verbatim on Slide 16.

2024:Q61.questionText: ____ resources refer to the machines used during the manufacturing process.
2024:Q61.explanation: In the breakdown of organizational resources, 'Assets/Capital' (or Capital resources) specifically refer to the equipment, facilities, and machines that are utilized as inputs in the production process to create goods or services.
2024:Q61.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer supported by Slide 13 and the diagram on Slide 14.

2024:Q62.questionText: This role performed by Trot can be called
2024:Q62.context: Trot is the CEO of a consulting firm. He plays a key role in guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2024:Q62.explanation: Influencing is formally defined as the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2024:Q62.reference: Chapter 15: Influencing and Communication - Answer found on Slide 3.

2024:Q63.questionText: Organizational communication that does not follow the lines of the organizational chart is specifically called
2024:Q63.explanation: Informal organizational communication (the grapevine) springs up irregularly, is not controlled by top executives, and thus does not follow the formal lines of the organizational chart.
2024:Q63.reference: Chapter 15: Influencing and Communication - Answer found on Slide 22.

2024:Q64.questionText: ____ skills are very important to managers at the lower, middle and top levels.
2024:Q64.explanation: According to the classic view charts of management skills, while the need for technical and conceptual skills varies greatly depending on the management level, 'Human Skills' occupy an equally large and consistent segment across top, middle, and supervisory levels.
2024:Q64.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer found on the visual charts on Slide 23 and Slide 24.

2024:Q65.questionText: This is a fault in the ____ function of management.
2024:Q65.context: Gayle has not established appropriate performance standards for her team.
2024:Q65.explanation: Establishing performance standards is a core component of the "Comparing Measured Performance To Standards" step within the Controlling process. Failing to establish these standards prevents successful controlling.
2024:Q65.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer deduced from Slide 11.

2024:Q66.questionText: The more resources unused during the production process, the more ____ the manager.
2024:Q66.explanation: Managerial efficiency deals directly with the proportion of resources contributing to productivity. A higher proportion of unused or wasted resources means fewer resources are actively contributing to the final product, rendering the manager inefficient.
2024:Q66.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer found on Slide 16 and Slide 17.

2025:Q1.questionText: Controlling does not highlight the deviations in the process.
2025:Q1.explanation: The entire purpose of comparing measured performance to standards is to highlight deviations (whether performance is "significantly different from standards") so that corrective action can be taken.
2025:Q1.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer deduced from the Controlling Process diagram on Slide 8.

2025:Q2.questionText: Organizing is the process of establishing orderly uses for all resources within the management system.
2025:Q2.explanation: This is the exact, verbatim definition of organizing provided in the fundamental definitions of the lecture.
2025:Q2.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer found verbatim on Slide 5.

2025:Q3.questionText: Vertical dimensioning is directly related to the concept of the scalar relationship that is, the chain of command.
2025:Q3.explanation: Vertical dimensioning is the extent to which an organization uses vertical levels, which directly relates to the scalar relationship (chain of command) where authority scales downward.
2025:Q3.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer found directly on Slide 18 and Slide 19.

2025:Q4.questionText: Corrective actions are necessary after analyzing the deviations.
2025:Q4.explanation: If the comparison step shows that performance is "significantly different from standards" (a deviation), the immediate next required step in the controlling process is to "Take corrective action".
2025:Q4.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer found directly on the Controlling Process diagram on Slide 8.

2025:Q5.questionText: Human skills, unlike technical skills, involve the ability to see the organization as a whole.
2025:Q5.explanation: The ability to see the organization as a whole is defined as 'Conceptual Skills', whereas 'Human Skills' deal with the ability to work effectively with people.
2025:Q5.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer found on Slide 22.

2025:Q6.questionText: An organization that wants to retain an employee may need to assist that employee's spouse in his or her career development as well.
2025:Q6.explanation: Although not explicitly stated in the provided slides, this is a known external HR concept related to dual-career couples and employee retention strategies. Often, retaining a highly valued employee who is relocating requires assisting their trailing spouse with career placement. *Note: If constrained strictly to the slides, there is no direct evidence for this, but it is a standard true/false question in management courses.*
2025:Q6.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Standard HR Management principle (Not explicitly detailed in the provided slides, but generally considered True in this course context).

2025:Q7.questionText: The supply of individuals from which to recruit is continually changing, which means that at times, finding appropriate human resources will be much harder than at other times.
2025:Q7.explanation: The lecture slides explicitly state that the supply of individuals to recruit from is continually changing, making finding appropriate human resources harder at certain times. Because of this, HR specialists must continually monitor the labor market.
2025:Q7.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer found verbatim on Slide 10.

2025:Q8.questionText: Wikstrom's human resource inventory forms are meant to be used exclusively for filling managerial positions and cannot be used for filling nonmanagerial positions.
2025:Q8.explanation: While Wikstrom's specific examples (Management Inventory Card) focus on managers, the overarching goal of an HR Inventory is to evaluate the characteristics of 'organization members' (past performance and future potential) to fill positions from within. Modern succession planning tools are deployed for 'employees' broadly, not exclusively managers.
2025:Q8.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer deduced from Slide 13 and Slide 18.

2025:Q9.questionText: A task group is a formal group outlined in the chain of command on an organization chart.
2025:Q9.explanation: A group outlined in the chain of command is a 'Command Group', whereas a 'Task Group' is formed for nonroutine tasks.
2025:Q9.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 9.

2025:Q10.questionText: The membership of friendship groups in an organization tend to remain static over long periods of time.
2025:Q10.explanation: Informal groups like friendship groups are not established by management decree and tend to change as personal affiliations, work locations, and employee turnover occur. They are generally dynamic, not static.
2025:Q10.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition of informal groups on Slide 6 and general management theory.

2025:Q11.questionText: A people-related step in building an effective team is setting stable goals and priorities for the team.
2025:Q11.explanation: Setting goals and priorities is typically considered a procedural or task-oriented step, not a people-oriented guideline. People-oriented guidelines involve rephrasing ideas, ensuring participation, and stimulating thought.
2025:Q11.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 14 (Procedural) vs Slide 15 (People-Oriented).

2025:Q12.questionText: Henri Fayol recommends that businesses establish multiple guiding authorities when organizing resources.
2025:Q12.explanation: Henri Fayol's General Principles of Management explicitly include 'Unity of Command' and 'Unity of Direction'. These principles dictate that employees should receive orders from only one superior and that there should be one head and one unified plan for a group of activities having the same objective. Therefore, establishing multiple guiding authorities contradicts Fayol's framework.
2025:Q12.reference: Chapter 2: History and Current Thinking - Answer found on Slide 13 under General Principles of Management.

2025:Q13.questionText: Span of management refers to the number of organizational levels below that of a particular manager's.
2025:Q13.explanation: Span of management describes how many individuals a manager directly supervises, not the number of organizational levels below them. Organizational levels dictate the chart's 'height'.
2025:Q13.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer deduced from Slide 20 and Slide 23.

2025:Q14.questionText: According to the concept of corporate social responsibility, managers should regard societal goals as more important than organizational goals.
2025:Q14.explanation: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) obligates managers to take actions that protect and improve both the welfare of society and the interests of the organization simultaneously, rather than prioritizing societal goals over organizational goals. The slides emphasize balancing corporate health with stakeholder relations, ensuring an opportunity to make a "fair profit" alongside fulfilling societal needs.
2025:Q14.reference: Chapter 3: Business Ethics - Answer deduced from the principles of stakeholder relations and fair profit on Slide 9.

2025:Q15.questionText: A programmed decision is typically a one-shot structured decision.
2025:Q15.explanation: A programmed decision is 'routine and repetitive'. A 'one-shot decision' defines a non-programmed decision.
2025:Q15.reference: Chapter 8: Making Decisions - Answer found on Slide 5.

2025:Q16.questionText: What is the main purpose of the management by exception concept?

options.content: To focus on minor variances for operational improvements.
To minimize management's involvement in all business operations.
To involve management in every decision regarding business direction.
To notify management only of significant variances from planned results.

2025:Q16.explanation: While 'Management by exception' is not explicitly defined in the provided Chapter 21 slides, it is a core controlling concept closely tied to the flowchart on Slide 8: a manager only intervenes (Takes corrective action) when "Performance [is] significantly different from standards".
2025:Q16.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Deduced from the Controlling Process diagram on Slide 8.

2025:Q17.questionText: Which of the following features is of Formal organization -:

options.content: Directed by company rules and regulations

2025:Q17.explanation: A formal organization refers strictly to the designated relationships and structures explicitly outlined by management, which are directed by official company rules and regulations.
2025:Q17.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer derived from the definition of Formal Structure on Slide 16.

2025:Q18.questionText: Name one of the basic concepts for smoothly running an organisation.

options.content: None of the options is correct

2025:Q18.explanation: Management is the core encompassing concept whose primary role is to smoothly guide the organization towards its goals through the effective use of resources.
2025:Q18.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer supported by the definitions on Slide 4 and Slide 5.

2025:Q19.questionText: Organizing is the process of _____ the activities of an enterprise and _____
2025:Q19.explanation: Organizing essentially involves defining (identifying and dividing work into major tasks) and grouping them (departmentalization) to establish an orderly use of resources.
2025:Q19.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer deduced from the Organizing Process steps on Slide 7 and Departmentalizing concepts on Slide 24.

2025:Q20.questionText: At what step of the planning can be processed with the topmost and applicable plan would be implemented
2025:Q20.explanation: Selecting the best alternative (or 'selecting up objective' based on the flawed wording of the option) is the step where the most applicable plan is chosen for implementation.
2025:Q20.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the definition of planning on Slide 4 (selecting among opportunities to reach objectives).

2025:Q21.questionText: In HRM, what does the term "training and development" refer to?
2025:Q21.explanation: Training is defined as 'developing qualities in human resources' to make them more productive, and determining training needs involves identifying the 'information or skill areas of an individual/group that need further development'.
2025:Q21.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer based on the definitions on Slide 31 and Slide 33.

2025:Q22.questionText: It is the process of ensuring that events conform to plans.
2025:Q22.explanation: The lecture provides the strict definition: "Control: Ensuring that an event occurs as it was planned to occur".
2025:Q22.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer found verbatim on Slide 4.

options.content: Framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed

2025:Q23.explanation: Structure is the designated relationships among all resources of the management system, facilitating the use of each resource individually and collectively. This encompasses both the managerial hierarchy and the operating tasks performed by employees.
2025:Q23.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer derived from the definition and purpose of Structure on Slide 16.

2025:Q24.questionText: In which pace of the planning process, two sides of a coin of each alternative are examined.
2025:Q24.explanation: Evaluating alternatives is the step where the pros and cons of different courses of action are analyzed before a final choice is made.
2025:Q24.reference: Chapter 8: Making Decisions - Slide 16 covers evaluating alternatives before selection.

options.content: The last function of the manager
None of the options is correct

2025:Q25.explanation: Due to the concept of Primacy of Planning, it is the foundational and primary function that precedes organizing, influencing, and controlling.
2025:Q25.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer found on Slide 7 (Primacy of Planning).

2025:Q26.questionText: The controlling function is performed by
2025:Q26.explanation: Although not explicitly on a single slide in Chapter 21, the controlling process requires that "managers" perform it. Based on the overarching principles of management (e.g., Chapter 1), all levels of management—top, middle, and lower—execute all four fundamental functions (Planning, Organizing, Influencing, Controlling).
2025:Q26.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Inferred from the general use of "managers" throughout the slides and fundamental management theory.

2025:Q27.questionText: Thinking for the future output is known as

options.content: All of the options are correct

2025:Q27.explanation: Developing or setting planning premises involves making assumptions and forecasts about future conditions that will affect the execution of the plans.
2025:Q27.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the definition of planning on Slide 4 (assumptions about future conditions for action programs).

2025:Q28.questionText: What is the point of distinction between formal and informal organization

options.content: The managers are the leaders in case of formal organization while in case of informal organization the managers may or may not be the leaders and the leaders are chosen by the groups
Formal organization is flexible in nature while informal is rigid in nature

2025:Q28.explanation: Formal structures are outlined explicitly by management, placing appointed managers as the structural leaders. Informal structures develop organically from informal activities, meaning leaders emerge naturally from the group. Option B is incorrect as formal structures tend to be more rigid than informal ones.
2025:Q28.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer deduced from the definitions of Formal and Informal structures on Slide 16.

2025:Q29.questionText: ______ is the management function through which managers compare present performance to preestablished performance standards.
2025:Q29.explanation: Controlling is the process of comparing performance to predetermined standards to see if performance aligns.
2025:Q29.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer found on Slide 6 under Mockler's definition.

2025:Q30.questionText: In the context of the personnel function, what is the significance of job analysis?
2025:Q30.explanation: Job analysis is a technique used to gain an understanding of a job, specifically for the purpose of creating a job description (which lists specific activities/duties) and a job specification (human qualifications). It essentially defines the role and its responsibilities.
2025:Q30.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer found on Slide 7 and Slide 8.

2025:Q31.questionText: Controlling function brings the management cycle back to the
2025:Q31.explanation: Controlling involves checking performance against plans. If corrective action is needed, the process flows back to "change plans, organization, or influencing methods". Because Planning and Control are "inseparable functions" (Siamese twins), controlling naturally feeds directly back into planning to adjust future standards.
2025:Q31.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer deduced from Slide 4 and the flowchart on Slide 8.

2025:Q32.questionText: Looking after the change in an organizational environment doesn't come with any surprises. Address importance of planning related to the topic:

options.content: Planning reduces the risk of uncertainties

2025:Q32.explanation: The protective purpose of planning is specifically designed to minimize risk by reducing uncertainties surrounding business conditions, thereby preventing surprises in a changing environment.
2025:Q32.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer found directly on Slide 5 under 'Protective' purpose.

2025:Q33.questionText: Which HRM function is responsible for recruiting and selecting employees?
2025:Q33.explanation: The phrasing of the question is somewhat tautological. The process of recruiting and selecting employees falls directly under the 'Recruitment and Selection' (or 'Providing Human Resources') function of HRM, which encompasses Step 1: Recruitment and Step 2: Selection.
2025:Q33.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Slide 26 defines selection in the HRM process.

2025:Q34.questionText: Which one is a type of Organizational structures
2025:Q34.explanation: Functional structure (departmentalization based on function) is a primary type of organizational structure outlined in the lecture, alongside product, geographic, customer, and matrix structures.
2025:Q34.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer found on Slide 25 (Departments Based on Function).

2025:Q35.questionText: Which of the following statements does not highlight the relationship between planning and controlling

options.content: Planning and controlling are separable twins of management.
Planning without controlling is meaningless; controlling without planning is blind.
Planning is prescriptive, controlling is evaluative.
Planning and controlling are interrelated and interdependent.

2025:Q35.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that planning and control are "virtually inseparable functions" and calls them the "Siamese twins of management". Therefore, stating they are "separable" is false and does not highlight their true relationship.
2025:Q35.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer found directly on Slide 4.

2025:Q36.questionText: The process of organizing involves following steps A. Identification and division of work, B. Assignment of duties, C. Establishing reporting relationship, D. Departmentalization (Arrange them in correct order)
2025:Q36.explanation: The logical sequence of organizing starts with identifying and dividing the work into manageable tasks (A), grouping those activities into departments (D), assigning specific duties to individuals (B), and finally establishing reporting relationships or a chain of command (C).
2025:Q36.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer logically follows the Organizing Process sequence from establishing tasks to allocating directives on Slide 7.

2025:Q37.questionText: Which of the following would be considered a formal group?

options.content: task force for employee birthday celebrations
bringing people from various functions to solve a business dilemma

2025:Q37.explanation: A group formed by management to solve a business dilemma (a nonroutine task) is a formal "Task Group." Birthday, reading, and bowling groups are informal interest or friendship groups.
2025:Q37.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Based on the definition of Task Group on Slide 9.

2025:Q38.questionText: ______ can be defined as guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2025:Q38.explanation: Influencing is formally defined as the process of guiding the activities of organization members in appropriate directions.
2025:Q38.reference: Chapter 15: Influencing and Communication - Answer found on Slide 3.

2025:Q39.questionText: The information the receiver gets is called
2025:Q39.explanation: The encoded information that the source shares and that the destination (receiver) derives meaning from is called the message.
2025:Q39.reference: Chapter 15: Influencing and Communication - Answer found on Slide 12 and Slide 14.

2025:Q40.questionText: Which of the following is not important for controlling function?

options.content: It helps in judging the accuracy of standards.

2025:Q40.explanation: Controlling ensures events occur as planned, which promotes coordination. Therefore, "restricting coordination" is false and not an important or intended outcome of the controlling function.
2025:Q40.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Deduced from the definition of control on Slide 4.

2025:Q41.questionText: Identify the correct sequence of the steps involved in the controlling process.

options.content: Measurement of actual performance, Taking corrective action, Setting performance standards, Comparison of actual performance with standards, Analysing deviations
Comparison of actual performance with standards, Setting performance standards. Measurement of actual performance, Analysing deviations, Taking corrective action
Setting performance standards, Measurement of actual performance, Comparison of actual performance with standards, Analysing deviations, Taking corrective action
Taking corrective action, Measurement of actual performance, Comparison of actual performance with standards, Analysing deviations, Setting performance standards

2025:Q41.explanation: Standards must be set first (usually during planning/initial control setup). Then the formal controlling process steps follow: 1. Measuring Performance, 2. Comparing Measured Performance To Standards (which involves analyzing deviations), 3. Taking Corrective Action. Option 'c' perfectly outlines this logical progression.
2025:Q41.reference: Chapter 21: Controlling Fundamentals - Answer deduced from the list of steps on Slide 9 and the definition of a Standard on Slide 11.

2025:Q42.questionText: ______ includes determining tasks and groupings of work. It should not be rigid, but adaptable and flexible to meet challenges as circumstances change.
2025:Q42.explanation: Organizing involves establishing tasks and forming departments (groupings of work). Henri Fayol advised that strict adherence to formal structures is not always advisable, highlighting the need for adaptability and flexibility in organizing.
2025:Q42.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer aligns with Departmentalizing (Slide 24) and Fayol's advice on flexibility (Slide 35).

2025:Q43.questionText: At what stage of the planning becomes the most feasible plan that can be implemented.
2025:Q43.explanation: Selecting the best alternative is the stage where the most feasible course of action is chosen to be developed into actual implemented plans.
2025:Q43.reference: Chapter 8: Making Decisions - Slide 16 covers selecting the most beneficial alternative.

2025:Q44.explanation: A standard is a "level of activity established to serve as a model for evaluating organizational performance". Because "20%" is a specific, numerical metric, it represents a quantitative standard.

2025:Q45.questionText: Which of the following is a method used in group or organisational training needs assessment?

options.content: Consideration of current and projected changes

2025:Q48.questionText: ______ are work groups established by the organization that have designate work assignments and specific tasks.
2025:Q48.explanation: Formal groups are defined as existing within an organization by virtue of management decree to perform specific tasks. While "task groups" is a subset, "formal groups" is the broader, correct umbrella term for groups established by the organization with designated assignments.
2025:Q48.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Found on Slide 6.

2025:Q49.questionText: Which term refers to the process of evaluating and improving employee performance?
2025:Q49.explanation: Performance Appraisal is explicitly defined as the 'process of reviewing individuals' past productive activity to evaluate the contribution they have made'. Its purpose is to furnish feedback to help them become more productive (improve performance).
2025:Q49.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer found verbatim on Slide 41.

2025:Q50.questionText: Which one of the following is among the steps of Organizing -
2025:Q50.explanation: Organizing involves allocating directives and resources, which encompasses both the assignment of duties to specific roles and the establishment of reporting relationships (the chain of command).
2025:Q50.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer derived from Step 4 of the Organizing Process (Slide 7) and Scalar Relationships (Slide 19).

2025:Q51.questionText: Planning establishes a ground standard for
2025:Q51.explanation: Planning sets the objectives and standards that the controlling function later uses to measure actual performance against.
2025:Q51.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the connection between Planning and Controlling on Slide 7.

2025:Q52.questionText: It helps to cross the gap between the current position and the future
2025:Q52.explanation: Planning is defined as determining how the organization can get where it wants to go (future position) from its current position.
2025:Q52.reference: Chapter 7: Principles of Planning - Answer supported by the definition of planning on Slide 4.

2025:Q53.questionText: which of the following is an advantage of Functional structure

options.content: Functional structure leads to occupational specialization
Functional structure promotes better control and coordination within the department

2025:Q53.explanation: Departmentalization based on function intrinsically groups people with similar skills, leading to occupational specialization. Additionally, placing power in functional heads promotes consistency, which improves control and coordination within that specific department.
2025:Q53.reference: Chapter 11: Fundamentals of Organizing - Answer derived from the advantages of Departments Based on Function on Slide 26.

2025:Q54.explanation: Basic managerial activities—specifically people-related and task-related skills—encompass supervising (monitoring operations), motivating (which is the core of the 'influencing' function), and stimulating personnel to reach organizational goals efficiently.
2025:Q54.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer supported by the concepts on Slide 10 and Slide 27.

2025:Q55.questionText: The actual achievements compared with the objectives of the job is
2025:Q55.explanation: Comparing actual productive activity (achievements) against the management system objectives is the process of reviewing Job Performance during a Performance Appraisal. A job description merely lists the duties, and job evaluation is a method to determine compensation.
2025:Q55.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer deduced from the definition of Performance Appraisal on Slide 41.

2025:Q56.questionText: Which performance appraisal methods consumes a lot of time?
2025:Q56.explanation: While specific methods are not explicitly detailed in the provided slides, in standard HRM theory, the 'Essay method' requires the evaluator to write a detailed narrative describing the employee's performance, which is highly time-consuming compared to simply checking boxes on a Rating Scale.
2025:Q56.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Standard HR Management principle (Not explicitly detailed in the provided slides, but a standard answer in HRM courses).

2025:Q57.questionText: Which of the following is a benefit of employee training?

options.content: Helps people identify with organisational goals
Provides a good climate for learning, growth and co - ordination

2025:Q57.explanation: Training is defined as developing qualities in human resources to make them more productive. By utilizing techniques like Programmed Learning, Coaching, and Position Rotation, training inherently provides a climate for learning and growth. *Note: While 'a' and 'b' can be secondary effects, 'c' is the most direct benefit of a structured learning program.*
2025:Q57.reference: Chapter 13: Human Resource Management - Answer supported by the 'Techniques for Transmitting Information' and 'Developing Skills' on Slides 36-39.

2025:Q58.questionText: Which of the following statements about groupthink is true?

options.content: Groupthink cannot take place in a newly formed group.
A group with high levels of mistrust and conflicts is likely to be most susceptible to groupthink.
A group with a high level of cohesiveness is likely to be susceptible to groupthink.
Managers must help committees to establish groupthink to generate alternative problem solutions.
A group which is highly competitive will most probably result in groupthink.

2025:Q58.explanation: Groupthink happens when the desire for agreement dominates the group. A highly cohesive group is naturally more driven by agreement and conformity, making it highly susceptible to groupthink.
2025:Q58.reference: Chapter 18: Groups and Teams - Inferred from the definition and symptoms of Groupthink on Slide 16.

2025:Q59.questionText: Which of the following statements is true for the management function?

options.content: It reaches goals by working with and through people.
It is a one-time function in an organization.
It is a series of continuing and unrelated activities.
It involves and concentrates on reaching individual goals.
It does not consider the people aspect of organizations.

2025:Q59.explanation: Management is formally defined as the process of reaching organizational goals by working with and through people and other organizational resources.
2025:Q59.reference: Chapter 1: Introduction - Answer found verbatim on Slide 5.

2025:Q60.questionText: Which of the following is an error managers make during the planning stage of management?

options.content: not emphasizing coordination of organization members
not exploring enough viable alternatives for reaching objectives
not monitoring progress in carrying out plans
not taking the time to communicate properly with organization members

2025:Q60.explanation: In Chapter 1, common mistakes for each function were defined. The mistake of 'not exploring enough viable alternatives for reaching objectives' is a specific error associated with the Planning function. Establishing departments is Organizing, communicating is Influencing, and monitoring is Controlling.
